subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Bioremediation: Using Life to Clean Pollution
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bioremediation: Using Life to Clean Pollution usable.

hook.text: Oil-eating bacteria cleaned up the 2010 Gulf oil spill faster than any human technology. Nature had its own cleanup crew.

buildup.text: Bioremediation uses living organisms — bacteria, fungi, plants — to break down or absorb pollutants from soil and water.

discovery.text: Mycoremediation uses fungi. Oyster mushrooms break down diesel fuel. Their enzymes split hydrocarbons into harmless compounds.

twist.text: Phytoremediation uses plants to absorb heavy metals. Sunflowers at Chernobyl pulled cesium and strontium from contaminated soil.

climax.text: Engineered bacteria could target specific pollutants. Synthetic biology may create microbes that eat plastic, PCBs, or PFAS.

punchline.text: Pollute with chemistry. Clean with biology. Nature has the enzymes.

quiz.question: How were sunflowers used after the Chernobyl disaster?
options: Their tall stalks were used to measure radiation levels across the exclusion zone
They were planted to absorb cesium and strontium from contaminated soil
Their seeds provided food for wildlife returning to the abandoned area
